Desktops.Title: Virtual desktops
Desktops.Explanation: The documented Windows interface can only read the desktop of a window, tell whether it is on the current desktop, and move windows owned by this application. Enumerating desktops, switching to a numbered desktop and pinning need the advanced backend, which is not part of this build.
Desktops.NamesExplanation: Rename them here. The names are saved and put back if Windows loses the desktops.
Rules.Hint: Rules are read from rules.json. The check box is saved immediately.
Hotkeys.Hint: Hotkeys are read from hotkeys.json. A combination already taken by another application is shown as a conflict.
Settings.StartWithWindows: Start Virtual Desk Manager with Windows
Settings.FollowMovedWindow: Follow the window after moving it to another desktop
Settings.ApplyRulesOnStartup: Apply the rules to the windows already open at start up
About.Description: Advanced virtual desktop and window manager for Windows 11. Runs as a standard user: no administrator rights, no driver, no DLL injection.
About.TrayNote: Closing this window keeps the application running in the tray. Use Exit in the tray menu to stop it completely.
Settings.ShowTitleBarButton: Show a button on the title bar of the active window
Settings.ShowDesktopInTray: Show the current desktop on the tray icon
RuleEditor.PinApplication: Show the application on all desktops
RuleEditor.NewInstance: Open a new window even if it is already open on another desktop
RuleEditor.NewInstanceHint: Left alone, Virtual Desk Manager asks whether to go to the desktop where it already is or stay here.
Overlay.RequiresAdvancedBackend: Needs the advanced backend, which is not part of this build.
Overlay.RuleSaved: From now on, {0} opens like this.
Tray.AlwaysOpenHere: Always open the active window here
Follow.Question: {0} opened on {1}. Go there?
Settings.AskToFollowRuleMoves: When a rule opens an application on another desktop, ask whether to go there
HotkeyEditor.Press: Click here and press the keys
HotkeyEditor.Conflict: «{0}» is already taken by «{1}» ({2}). Using it here switches that one off.
Hotkeys.Displaced: «{1}» ({0}) has been switched off: it lost its combination.
RuleEditor.ApplicationHint: Pick it from the ones you have open. You do not need to know what its file is called.
RuleEditor.NoApplications: Nothing matches that. Open the application and reopen this window, or fill it in by hand below.
RuleEditor.ReuseExistingWindow: Go to the window this application already has
RuleEditor.ReuseExistingWindowHint: When the application is already open, go to its window and ask the newly opened one to close. Only for applications that insist on a new window every time. It asks, so anything unsaved can still be saved.
Validation.HotkeyDuplicateId: Another shortcut already uses that identifier.
Validation.HotkeyNeedsModifier: Without Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win this key stops working in every other program while the shortcut exists.
Validation.HotkeyWindowsKeyOftenReserved: Windows keeps many Win+key combinations for itself. If this is one of them it will be saved but show as not registered in the list.
Validation.HotkeyDuplicateCombination: Another shortcut already uses that combination.
Validation.RuleInvalidRegex: That regular expression is not valid.
Command.MoveWindowLeft: Move window to the previous desktop
Command.MoveWindowRight: Move window to the next desktop
Settings.ConsoleEnabled: Enable the console that drops from the top of the screen
Settings.ConsoleHideOnFocusLost: Roll it back up when it stops being the window in front
Settings.ConsoleFollowMouse: Drop the console on the screen where the mouse is
Console.Pin: Pin: keep it down when another window takes the focus
Grid.Hint: Click to go there · Drag onto another desktop to move it · The cross closes the window · Esc to close · Right-click a desktop to rename or remove it
Status.Unsupported: Not available with the active backend.
Status.AccessDenied: Windows denied access to that window.
Status.InvalidWindow: The window is no longer there.
Settings.BackupExplanation: OneDrive and Google Drive are folders. Virtual Desk Manager writes an 8 KB file into the one you pick and your own client uploads it: no account, no sign in, nothing to authorise.
Settings.BackupAutomatic: Keep a copy of how things were before each change
Settings.BackupNoCloudFound: Neither OneDrive nor Google Drive was found on this computer.
Settings.BackupCopyToCloud: Copy there too whenever the configuration changes
Backup.Title: Restore configuration
Backup.Hint: Pick a copy and its configuration goes back in place. What you have now is saved first, so you can always come back.
Backup.ConfirmRestore:
Your whole configuration will be replaced by the copy from {0}.

What you have now is saved first, so you can undo this.

Go ahead?
Backup.SavedWithCloud: Copy saved, and into {0} as well
Backup.Empty: That file does not hold any configuration.
HotkeyEditor.SecondCombinationHint: A second way to trigger the same action, for when the first one is awkward from where your hand is.
Validation.HotkeySameCombinationTwice: Both combinations are the same one, so there is still only one way to trigger it.
Settings.TitleBarButtonOffsetHint: Applications that draw their own title bar (browsers, Electron) sometimes put things where the button lands. This shifts it further left until it is clear of them.
Command.MoveWindowToZone: Move the window to a zone
Settings.WindowLayoutExplanation: When the computer sleeps or locks, the screens switch off, Windows is left with one and piles every window onto it. This remembers where each window was for each set of screens, so when the screens come back the windows do too.
Settings.WindowLayoutRestoreAutomaticall: Put them back when the screens return or the computer wakes
Settings.WindowLayoutRestoreOnStartup: Put them back when the application starts too
Settings.WindowLayoutNoneForThese: Nothing saved yet for the screens you have right now.
Diary.Hint: What is happening, live: if something does not work, this shows why. If the log file is turned off below, nothing will appear here.
Zones.Title: Zones for each monitor
Zones.Explanation: Split each monitor into zones and send a window to one with a shortcut. Every monitor gets its own split: what fits on an ultrawide does not fit on the laptop next to it.
Zones.HotkeysAdded: {0} shortcuts added. They are in Keyboard shortcuts.
Zones.SnapWhileDragging: Snap into a zone while dragging with Shift
Zones.SnapHint: Hold Shift while dragging a window: the zones appear, and where you let go is where the window lands.
Zones.SeamlessEdgesHint: Windows 11 rounds the corners and paints a one-pixel edge around every window, so two windows touching to the pixel still show a grey line between them. Each window gets its own back when you turn this off or close the application.
Settings.InterceptReserved: Take over the combinations Windows keeps for itself
Settings.InterceptReservedHint: Windows refuses to hand over its own shortcuts, such as Ctrl+Esc. A low-level keyboard hook sees them before the shell does, which is how PowerToys and AutoHotkey do it. It is only used for what Windows has refused. It will not work while a window running as administrator is in front, because Windows does not let an ordinary program take its keys, and Ctrl+Alt+Del and Win+L are out of reach for anyone.
TaskbarBadges.Explanation: Puts a badge on each taskbar button showing which desktop that application is open on, so you can tell where something is without going to look for it. It does not touch the taskbar: it is drawn on top and lets clicks through.
TaskbarBadges.Enabled: Mark which desktop each application is on
TaskbarBadges.HideWhenCurrent: Do not mark what is already on this desktop
TaskbarBadges.Legend: A number is the desktop the application is on. “…” means it has windows on several at once, and “∞” that it is pinned and shows on all of them.
TaskbarBadges.FilterWarning: Windows is showing only this desktop's windows on the taskbar, so an application open on another desktop has no button to mark and you will only see badges on pinned icons. To see them all: Settings › System › Multitasking › “Show all open windows” › “On all desktops”.
Vdesk.DesktopsHint: Switch desktop with a click, name them, and drag a window from one to another to move it.
Desktops.RemoveOneWindow: Its window will move to “{0}”. Nothing is closed.
Desktops.RemoveWindows: Its {0} windows will move to “{1}”. None of them is closed.
Desktops.RemoveOneRule: One automation uses this desktop: check it so it sends its application somewhere else.
Desktops.RemoveRules: {0} automations use this desktop: check them so they send their applications somewhere else.
Desktops.RemovedWithWindows: Removed “{0}”. Its windows are now on “{1}”.
Desktops.RemoveLast: Windows needs at least one desktop: the last one cannot be removed.
Desktops.RemoveUnsupported: Desktops cannot be removed in basic mode.
Vdesk.DesktopClickHint: Click to go to this desktop. Drop a window from another one here to bring it.
Vdesk.DesktopsMore: How desktops are switched, hotkeys and window layout are in Settings.
Diary.ClipboardBusy: The clipboard is in use by another application; try again.
Page.Home.Intro: How Virtual Desk Manager is doing right now, and what you use most, one click away.
Page.Home.Help: The front page. When something needs your attention (a shortcut that another application already uses, a configuration file with a mistake), it shows up here first, with a button to go and fix it.
Page.Desktops.Intro: Your virtual desktops, with a name for each one, and how you move between them.
Page.Desktops.Help: Virtual Desk Manager remembers the names of the desktops and puts them back if Windows loses them, which happens now and then after an update.
Page.Windows.Intro: The button Virtual Desk Manager adds to each window, the marks on the taskbar and where each window goes back to.
Page.Windows.Help: Everything Virtual Desk Manager draws on top of your windows and of the taskbar. None of it touches the windows themselves: it is drawn over them and lets the clicks through.
Page.Automations.Intro: What Virtual Desk Manager does on its own when an application opens a window.
Page.Automations.Help: Each automation says which windows it looks at (by program, title or window class) and what to do with them. If several match the same window, the one with the highest priority wins. You can also create one from the button on the title bar: «Always open this application».
Page.Zones.Intro: Split each screen into zones and fit windows into them with a shortcut, or by dragging them with Shift held down.
Page.Zones.Help: Each screen has its own layout: what fits on an ultrawide does not fit on the laptop next to it. Fitted windows can stay glued together, without the rounded corners and the thin edge of Windows 11, so that two windows side by side leave no line between them.
Page.Hotkeys.Intro: Virtual Desk Manager's key combinations, grouped by what they do.
Page.Hotkeys.Help: If another application already uses a combination, it is marked in red and Virtual Desk Manager cannot use it until you change it. Double-click a shortcut to change it: press «Edit» and then the new keys.
Page.Backup.Intro: Copies of your configuration, to undo a change or to take it to another computer.
Page.Backup.Help: A copy keeps the settings, the automations and the shortcuts. It does not keep open windows.
Page.General.Help: Closing this window does not close Virtual Desk Manager: it keeps running in the notification area, and you quit it from its menu there.
Page.Tools.Intro: What you need to find out why something is not working.
Page.Tools.Help: The diary shows what is happening, live. The technical details are folded at the bottom: you only need them to report a problem.
Page.Console.Intro: The console that drops down from the top of the screen with its shortcut, Quake-style.
Page.Console.Help: The shortcut that drops it down and folds it up is changed in Keyboard shortcuts. Width and height are a percentage of the screen, so the same settings work on any monitor.
Page.Help.Intro: First steps, what each thing is and what to do if something does not work.
Page.Help.Help: Point at the «i» of a setting for a short explanation, and press F1 for the long one: it explains the setting under the mouse or, if there is none, the whole section. To find any setting without knowing where it is, type in «Search a setting» (Ctrl+F).
Home.EngineBasic: Basic mode: some functions are not available
Home.AllGoodHint: When a shortcut cannot be used or a configuration file has a mistake, it will show up here with a button to go and fix it.
Home.QuickActionsHint: What you use most, without looking for it.
Attention.HotkeyConflict: The shortcut {0} ({1}) does not work: another application already uses it.
Group.TechnicalHint: Only needed to report a problem.
Row.FollowMovedWindow: If you move a window with a shortcut, you jump with it.
Row.ShowDesktopInTray: To know at a glance which one you are on.
Row.TitleBarButton: A small button next to minimise, with the window's menu.
Row.TitleBarButtonTip: From its menu: always on top, on every desktop, move to another desktop and always open this application this way.
Row.TaskbarBadges: A number on its taskbar button.
Row.WindowLayout: When the screens come back or the computer wakes up, every window goes back to its place.
Row.WindowLayoutDelay: How long the screens take to settle. Raise it if a window ends up in the wrong place.
Row.AutomationsList: The switch turns each one on or off on the spot. Double-click one to change it.
Row.PauseAutomationsHint: They stop being applied until you turn this off.
Row.ApplyOnStartup: Also apply them to the windows already open at start-up
Row.AskToFollow: Ask whether I want to go there when one takes an application to another desktop
Row.AskToFollowHint: If you turn it off, the application opens there and you stay where you are.
Row.Zones: If you turn it off, nothing below does anything.
Row.ZoneHotkeys: Creates a shortcut to send the window to each zone.
Row.HotkeysList: Double-click a shortcut to change it. The red ones do not work because another application already uses them.
Row.InterceptReserved: Such as Ctrl+Esc. Only needed if you want one of those.
Row.BackupAutomatic: One copy before each change, so you can always go back.
Row.YourCopiesHint: Save one now, go back to an earlier one, or take your configuration to another computer in a file.
Row.StartMinimized: Starts in the notification area, without opening this window.
Row.Configuration: Where Virtual Desk Manager keeps its configuration. «Reload configuration» reads it again from disk, after editing a file by hand.
Row.Console: Comes down from the top of the screen with its shortcut, and goes back up the same way.
Row.ConsolePin: With the pin on its bottom edge, or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+º, it stays down even when you switch to another window. Its shortcut still rolls it up.
Row.WriteLogFile: The diary is also kept in a file, to look at later.
Row.LogLevel: How much detail goes into the file. More detail only to look for a fault.
Row.Backend: How Virtual Desk Manager talks to the Windows desktops. If an update breaks it, Virtual Desk Manager switches to a basic mode and says so here.
Row.ActiveWindow: The window in front, as Virtual Desk Manager sees it.
Search.Title: Search
Search.None: Nothing with those words. Try another one, such as «screen», «keyboard» or «copy».
HelpPanel.F1Hint: F1: help for what you are looking at
HelpPanel.NoMore: No more explanation: it does what it says.
HelpPanel.PointAt: For help on one setting, point at it or select it and press F1.
HelpPage.FirstStepsText:
1. Name your desktops in My desktops.
2. Learn the shortcuts to move between them in Keyboard shortcuts.
3. Make each application open where you want it in Automations.
HelpPage.TroubleshootingText:
• A shortcut does nothing: another application uses it. In Keyboard shortcuts it is marked in red; change it.
• A window does not go to the desktop its automation says: in Tools › Diary, see whether the automation matches that window.
• Windows do not go back to their place when you plug the screen in: raise «Wait before rearranging» in Windows and appearance.
HelpPage.MapText:
For those who knew the old window, with its tabs:
• Dashboard → Home (status and warnings) and Tools › Technical details.
• Desktops → My desktops.
• Rules → Automations.
• Shortcuts → Keyboard shortcuts.
• Settings → split up: start-up and language in General; the title-bar button and window positions in Windows and appearance; pausing rules in Automations; Windows' reserved combinations in Keyboard shortcuts; the log in Tools.
• Zones → Arrange windows.
• Badges → Windows and appearance › Marks on the taskbar.
• Diary → Tools.
• Console → Console.
• Backups → Backups.
• About → General › About Virtual Desk Manager.
Update.Help: Virtual Desk Manager looks for new versions on its own at startup and once a day and lets you know in the tray. Unless you turn on "Install updates automatically", it never installs anything without asking. It downloads only what changed, checks the signature of every version before installing anything, and closes and reopens on its own.
Update.Available: There is a new version: {0}. You have {1}.
Update.AvailableHint: Install it from the notification area icon or in General › Updates.
Update.BadSignature: The update is not properly signed, so it is not installed.
Update.DownloadingInstaller: The installer is downloading in your browser.
Update.BadFile: A downloaded file is not the one it should be ({0}); nothing is installed.
Update.Restarting: Installing {0}: Virtual Desk Manager closes and opens again by itself.
Update.AutoHint: On startup and once a day, and lets you know when there is one.
Update.UpdatedText: It was installed automatically. What's new is in Settings › General.
Update.UpdatedTitle: Virtual Desk Manager has been updated to {0}
Update.ReadyWhenIdle: {0} is downloaded and will install itself when you are not using the computer.
Update.ReadyText: It will install itself when you stop using the computer for a while.
Update.InstallAutoHelp: With this on, Virtual Desk Manager looks for new versions every 4 hours and, if there is one, downloads it right away and checks its signature. To install it, it has to close and reopen for a few seconds, so it waits until you have not touched the keyboard or mouse for 3 minutes. When it reopens it tells you it has been updated. With "Receive test versions" on, it also installs betas. The standalone .exe cannot update itself: it lets you know and offers the installer.
Update.InstallAutoTip: It waits until you have not touched the keyboard or mouse for 3 minutes. Only in the installed Virtual Desk Manager, not in the standalone .exe.
Update.InstallAutoHint: Without asking: they are installed when you have not used the computer for a while.
Update.BetaHint: Betas: new things first, but they may fail.
Loading.Title: Loading…
Loading.Hint: It depends on your connection: it may take a few seconds.
Update.ErrorSecure: the update server has no valid secure connection right now. It is not a problem with this computer; try again later.
Update.ErrorNoConnection: could not reach the update server. Check the internet connection.
Update.ErrorServer: the update server answered with an error ({0}). Try again later.
